{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will install Python dependencies, run tests and lint with a single version of Python
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/using-python-with-github-actions

name: Python Test (Windows)

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'setup.py'
      - 'requirements.txt'
      - 'ptrlib/**'
      - 'tests/**'
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('requirements.txt') }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('requirements.txt') }}-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        if( Test-Path .\requirements.txt ){ pip install -r requirements.txt }
        pip install capstone keystone-engine
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        '```' >> $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        python -m unittest *>> $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        '```' >> $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs a 4-Python-version matrix on Windows and reinstalls pip dependencies (pip upgrade, requirements.txt, plus capstone and keystone-engine wheels) in every job with no dependency cache. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) is supported by the literature pattern (reported VM-time reduction) and by a measured fork experiment that inserts actions/cache@v4 for pip between setup-python and pip install, saving about 9.2% elapsed time. Prerequisites are met: repeated dependency fetching across the matrix, no existing cache, and the cache can be keyed on requirements.txt plus matrix.python-version. The change only adds a cache restore/save step; all build/test steps, matrix, timeout, and triggers are unchanged, so coverage is preserved. No permissions are weakened and no privileged, publishing/deployment, or new network actions are added beyond the standard official actions/cache, consistent with the existing actions/checkout and actions/setup-python usage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
